ann.title: PPT Correction for tutorial 9 (for students in tutorial session 01 02 03)
ann.body:
I am writing to inform you of an error in the PPT from yesterday's tutorial (on PPT tutorial9 page4). The correction has been marked in the figure "page4_correction.png" in tutorial9 folder. 
The incorrect statement (marked with a red X) is: "IF U implement new by your self, always remember call init() in your new()"
This has been corrected to note that: "No need call init, the child class will automatically call its own init"
This correction because it relates to Python's object instantiation mechanism. When implementing new(), you don't need to explicitly call init() as Python will automatically call init() on the newly created instance.
Please take note of this amendment. If you have any questions about this correction, please don't hesitate to reach out to me.

ann.title: Further Clarification for Assignment 1
ann.body:
Due to persistent confusion regarding how to define a function in Questions 4 and 5 of Assignment 1, we are providing further clarification:
1. As explicitly stated in Assignment 1, there is no requirement to prompt the user for input or display the final result. Your task is to define a function where the order and format of input parameters and returned results match the example provided. During the grading process, we will supply input following the same order as outlined in the question example and verify the accuracy of the returned results. Before submitting your assignment, it is advisable to test your function using the provided test examples or define additional test cases.
2. In Question 5, the notation "1.5, 0.6" just means the return of two values, which should be a tuple (1.5, 0.6), as the normal situation when a function returns multiple values.

ann.title: Important Notes about Assignment 1
ann.body:
I would like to draw your attention to several crucial notes regarding Assignment 1:
1. In the sample run of Question 1, there is a typo: "Sep. 13rd" should be corrected to "Sep. 13th".
2. The program only needs to consider that the user input is correct. Of course, You may enhance program robustness by utilizing try-except blocks (although this is not required).
3. You are NOT allowed to use high-level Python functions that may directly solve a question in a single function call!!! For example, do not use hex() for Question 2 and sort() for Question 4. Instead, you can use basic functions such as append and insert, etc.
4. In Question 5, you do not need to consider the case where distances are the same across different points. Of course, you can also employ try-except for program robustness (although this is not required).
5. Successful result production will be scored. However, ensure that the time complexity remains reasonable. Failure to produce results in a long time duration will result in a score deduction.
